scope: Voice and Capture scenes only. Native UI reconstructed from current Swift sources; no app code modified.

voice: The target is a magnified crop of Prosio's real Onboarding voice-practice view, not an invented messaging window. The outside caption identifies the crop.
Tabs use native 14pt text, 24pt gaps, and a 2pt accent underline. The input tab remains selected: selected-text voice editing does not automatically change the onboarding mode tab.
The practice card has a 14pt corner radius, a 14pt prompt, 24pt horizontal insets, a 21pt NSTextView, a 174pt native editor area, and a 12pt status/clear row.
The primary practice button is 40pt tall with an 8pt radius and RGB(0.29,0.36,0.52). Existing button/status labels are copied from the Swift UI.

The real HUD is a 36pt single-line capsule with 14pt horizontal padding, 8pt spacing, regular-material-like neutral fill, 0.5pt stroke and 6pt shadow. There is no large listening card, red waveform, permanent Fn hint, or separate success label inside it.
Listening uses eight 2.5pt black bars separated by 2.5pt, with height in 3...16pt. Preview text is 13pt, one line, head truncated, max 360pt. Finished insertion shows only a 13pt checkmark.
The edit mode chip is the exact pencil emoji used in HUDCapsuleView, on the native small neutral pill; it is deliberately not replaced with an unrelated glyph.

Fn key events start and stop recording; mouse events only focus and select the actual text area. Status, text insertion, selection, waveform phase and keyboard indication derive from the shared action table.

The sample is signed in and permission-ready. Its content is fictional demonstration text; native controls and layout come from the app. HUD and practice-view crop are arranged together for readability, with all pointer/control positions on one scale plane.
capture: The capture editor overlays frozen screen pixels; it is not a separate generic Mac document window. The source is fictional dark-background project content with the same light/dark typography treatment inspected in the installed-app translation fixtures.
The outside-selection shade is black at 28%; the selection has a 2pt system-blue border and eight blue 7pt resize handles.
Toolbar width is 404pt and height 42pt; it is a warm light capsule. Ink RGB is (0.37,0.35,0.32); surface RGB is (0.99,0.98,0.96). Hit areas are 28x30pt.

Primary tool order is selection, rectangle, ellipse, line, pen, text, redaction; the fixed right controls are translation, exit, pin, save JPEG, copy-and-exit. Copy is a dark circular control with a white doc.on.doc native SF Symbol.
The bounded primary-tool scroll area clips redo just as in the inspected 404pt native screenshot. Translation and output controls stay fixed.

Line is the toolbar entry for arrow drawing. The current native default preferredLineTool is arrow. Clicking line reveals the actual 350x118pt contextual palette with endpoint segmented control (none/arrow/tick), color swatches, width and opacity.
The arrow turns orange only after clicking the actual orange swatch. Orange is RGB(0.95,0.56,0.14); line width is 3pt, opacity 100%.
Toolbar is 12pt below the crop; the palette is 7pt below the toolbar because it fits in the viewport, matching CaptureInteractionGeometry.

Translation changes pixels only inside the capture editor after the translation-button action's processing delay. Copy output closes the editor after a four-frame asynchronous write and restores the untouched English source. No invented toast or persistent translation of the source app remains.
CapturePinnedWindow is borderless and image-only. Its source was checked to avoid adding any fabricated pin-preview window; this scene uses copy, so it does not show pinned UI.

The arrow endpoint segment is explicitly clicked at frame 183 even though the current Swift default is already arrow. This makes the visible drawing choice unambiguous and does not invent a different native default.
At arrow-end, the native AddAnnotationCommand selects the new arrow. Both 8x8pt white endpoint handles with 1.5pt system-blue borders appear, and the palette label becomes 已选中.
The last custom color well follows displayedAnnotationColor, so it becomes orange after the orange-color click rather than remaining red.

capture.heroCamera: h=progress(translate,16)*(1-progress(line-hover,13)); origin=(800-348h,221-67h); scale=1.5*(1+0.25h). UI and cursor are inside this same container.

stateBoundaries.selectionGeometry: The crop endpoint comes from interactionAt(min(frame,selection-end.frame)).x/y. It tracks the exact held pointer through frame 76 and remains fixed thereafter.
stateBoundaries.arrowGeometry: The arrow endpoint and both head vertices derive from interactionAt(min(frame,arrow-end.frame)).x/y, with no separate animation curve.
stateBoundaries.voiceSelectionGeometry: The selected line and width derive from the same held pointer used by InteractionCursor and freeze at select-end. Native text rows use 21pt font at 25.2pt line height.

qa.dataAttribute: data-action-target accepts whitespace-separated action IDs, including shared drag regions.
